Attest a capsule, binding a signature to what it covers

Source: R/attest.R
cpsatst.Rd

cpsatst() signs a manifest's canonical digest and records everything a verifier needs alongside it: the scheme, the public key, the context string, the pre-hash, a note and the time of signing. cpschkatst() checks the result against a manifest without being told anything further. Use them to publish a capsule together with proof that its manifest has not changed since you signed it.

Usage

cpsatst(man, key, ctx = NULL, prehash = "none", note = NULL)

cpschkatst(attest, man, keyexp = NULL, key = NULL)

Arguments

man

A manifest, as from mkmnf().

key

For cpsatst(), a signing key from fipskg() (ML-DSA, SLH-DSA and the other standardised schemes) or pqckg() (XMSS), or a shared secret (a string or raw vector) for "hmac". For cpschkatst(), the shared secret that checks an "hmac" attestation; it is not used for the other schemes, whose public key the attestation carries.

ctx

Optional context string (or raw vector), bound into the signature for the standardised schemes; see cpssign(). NULL (the default) means none.

prehash

Pre-hash, as in cpssign(). It is "none" (the default) or a hash name such as "sha256" or "sha512".

note

Optional free text recorded in the attestation – what the signature is meant to assert, in the signer's own words. It is covered by the signature, since it is part of the digest.

attest

An attestation from cpsatst().

keyexp

Optional public key the attestation must carry, as hex or as a key object from fipskg(), fipspubkey() or signpubkey(). Supply it when you know which key should have signed: without it the check confirms the attestation is internally consistent, which any key's holder could arrange.

Value

cpsatst() a list of class bricklayer_attestation with the character fields digest, scheme, public (hex), context, prehash, note and signed_utc (ISO 8601 UTC time), and signature (a bricklayer_signature from cpssign()).

cpschkatst() a list of class bricklayer_attestation_check with ok (logical) and checks, a data frame with columns check, ok and detail, one row per check.

Details

What this adds over cpssign(). A bare signature leaves three things implicit – which key, which scheme, and which bytes. A verifier who has to be told those out of band cannot check anything they were not already given, which makes the signature a formality. An attestation states them, so the check is cpschkatst(attestation, manifest) and nothing else.

What is signed: the payload digest (mnfdgst() of the manifest), scheme, public, ctx (hex for a raw context), prehash, note and signed_utc is put in canonical form (mnfcanon()) and its SHA-256 is signed with cpssign(). Every field, the note and the time included, is therefore covered: editing any of them breaks the signature. With an XMSS key from pqckg() the scheme is "xmss-sha256" and the context and pre-hash are not used by the signature; signing uses up one of the key's one-time indices, as every XMSS signature does.

With a shared secret (a string or raw vector) as key the scheme is "hmac": HMAC-SHA-256 under that secret, as cpssign(scheme = "hmac"). public is then a key id, the hex of HMAC-SHA-256 of the string "public" under the secret: it names the key, so keyexp can pin it, without revealing it. The secret itself is never recorded, so checking needs it again (key in cpschkatst()). context is "" and prehash "none", the bytes morie's capsule signer writes. HMAC is symmetric: anyone who can check the signature can also make one. It is not one of the post-quantum signature schemes and carries none of their guarantees.

The check, one row each: attestation_complete (every field is present), manifest_digest (the manifest's digest equals the attested one), key_as_expected (only when keyexp is given) and signature (the signature verifies under the attested public key; for "hmac", under key, whose key id must equal public). ok is TRUE when every row passes.

What it does NOT establish. That the public key belongs to whoever you think it does: an attestation is only as good as the channel the key arrived on, which is why keyexp exists. And that the manifest is true – only that it has not changed since it was signed. cpsfals() is for the other question. No chain seal is recorded; to attest a run history, sign chnseal() directly.

Errors: man not a list; key not from fipskg() or pqckg() and not a non-empty string or raw vector; an invalid prehash or ctx (from cpssign()), or either given with an HMAC key; attestation not from cpsatst(). A signature that fails to verify is a failed row, not an error.

See also

cpssign(), mnfdgst(), cpsfals(), chnseal().

Examples

m <- mkmnf(list(dataset = "otis", rows = 1200L), env = FALSE)
key <- fipskg("ML-DSA-65")
att <- cpsatst(m, key, note = "counts as published")
att
#> ╭── Capsule attestation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Scheme           ML-DSA-65                                                │
#> │   Manifest digest  efa1b7387f225380245de0b5170999e87ad4044f3e8fd2ef6a6bfbc2 │
#> │                    bd0a9c90                                                 │
#> │   Context          <none>                                                   │
#> │   Prehash          none                                                     │
#> │   Note             counts as published                                      │
#> │   Signed           2026-10-27T19:02:19Z                                     │
#> │   Public key       7110a46c93273dcf54f5a1abe5ac924e... (1952 bytes)         │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   A signed claim that a manifest with this digest was attested by the       │
#> │   holder of the key; check it against the manifest with cpschkatst().       │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# a verifier needs the attestation and the manifest, nothing else
res <- cpschkatst(att, m)
res$ok
#> [1] TRUE
res$checks
#>                  check   ok
#> 1 attestation_complete TRUE
#> 2      manifest_digest TRUE
#> 3            signature TRUE
#>                                                             detail
#> 1                                                                 
#> 2 efa1b7387f225380245de0b5170999e87ad4044f3e8fd2ef6a6bfbc2bd0a9c90
#> 3                                                                 

# any change to the manifest breaks it
m2 <- m
m2$meta$rows <- 1201L
cpschkatst(att, m2)$ok
#> [1] FALSE

# and so does presenting a different key
cpschkatst(att, m, keyexp = fipskg("ML-DSA-65")$public)$ok
#> [1] FALSE

# the note is signed too: editing it breaks the signature row
forged <- att
forged$note <- "counts corrected"
cpschkatst(forged, m)$checks[, c("check", "ok")]
#>                  check    ok
#> 1 attestation_complete  TRUE
#> 2      manifest_digest  TRUE
#> 3            signature FALSE

# a context string and a pre-hash
att2 <- cpsatst(m, key, ctx = "release 2026-10", prehash = "sha512")
cpschkatst(att2, m, keyexp = key)$ok
#> [1] TRUE

# a shared secret signs with HMAC; `public` is its key id, not the secret
att3 <- cpsatst(m, "shared-secret")
att3$public
#> [1] "4e289ef69cbe6f4c0d7de16c0801ad1155aba1598f2f4b25cddb46880caacd60"
cpschkatst(att3, m, key = "shared-secret", keyexp = att3$public)$ok
#> [1] TRUE
cpschkatst(att3, m, key = "another-secret")$checks[, c(
  "check",
  "ok",
  "detail"
)]
#>                  check    ok
#> 1 attestation_complete  TRUE
#> 2      manifest_digest  TRUE
#> 3            signature FALSE
#>                                                             detail
#> 1                                                                 
#> 2 efa1b7387f225380245de0b5170999e87ad4044f3e8fd2ef6a6bfbc2bd0a9c90
#> 3               the key given is not the key the attestation names

# a key that is not a signing key is refused
try(cpsatst(m, 42))
#> Error : `key` must come from fipskg() or pqckg(), or be a shared secret (a string or raw vector) for hmac
